## Body

Extends the immutable-route-counter note with F231 timing. active_us is nonparked handler wall time, not CPU time: SQLite/I/O, pool contention and scheduling remain active; detached/background work after a response is unmeasured. Rank route deltas, then correlate candidates with CPU/profile evidence rather than presenting timing sums as measured CPU utilization.

HeldSpan credits the task-local scope present at DROP, not a captured creator. Spawned tasks do not inherit it; moving a span can lose or misattribute held time. Keep spans sequential on the counted request future and narrow to deliberate parking, never database awaits. The current parks are inbox select, dispatch/canary wait, spawn footer, spawn registration and revive dead-pane settling. Per-request clamping guarantees held <= wall; it does not make cumulative atomic additions saturating.

Accounting cost scales with existing future polls and marked park/wake cycles as well as completed responses. A ready-request microbenchmark alone does not price long-poll wake accounting; retain source/compiler/profile provenance and distinguish pre-rebase binaries from exact-head test proof.

Evidence: security output 2026-11/20-verdict-pr-282-db3ae4d.dd.json; implementation in crates/daemon/src/http/route_counts.rs.
